before: Reversible magnesium deposition has been achieved both by weakening ion pairing and by bringing selected anions into the primary solvation shell. These effects can precede, accompany or persist independently of film formation. Representative studies illustrate distinct benefits, from suppressing amine reduction to opening a rearrangement pathway or preserving an active interface. We use these cases to define the evidence that separates population changes, molecular kinetics and retained surface effects. A two-state example clarifies why the abundance of a solvate and its reactivity are different quantities. We then propose controlled experiments and magnesium-specific modelling tests that connect local chemistry to both electrodes and material consumption. The aim is a reaction pathway that predicts electrolyte behaviour beyond the formulation in which it was discovered.
